claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a presbyter (priest) of the Church of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem lived in the first half of the fifth century and died after 451.
The homily titled 'On James (the Brother of the Lord) and David (Old Testament King and Prophet)' is Homily 10 in the collection of Hesychius's festal homilies.
The homily was written in Greek at Jerusalem in the early 5th century.
The homily was preached during the celebration of the saints held at the church of Holy Sion in Jerusalem on 25 December.

The occasion was a peculiar Jerusalem feast that, instead of celebrating the Nativity of Christ, dedicated 25 December to the commemoration of two of Christ's relatives: James, the so-called Brother of the Lord, and King David, Christ's ancestor.
This feast is recorded by the Armenian Lectionary of Jerusalem and Cosmas Indicopleustes (5.12).
Only a fragment of this homily is preserved, quoted in Photius' Bibliotheca, codex 275.
The preserved fragment shows Hesychius was aware the day was related to the Nativity and refers extensively to Bethlehem, as if trying to justify why Jerusalem does not join in the feast.
